english.title: Attempt to arrange / facilitate the commission of a child sex offence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) attempted to arrange or facilitate an act which you

(A)_[intended to do]_
(B)_[intended another person to do]_
(C)_[believed another person would do]_

in any part of the world, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), which would involve the commission of an offence under section

(D)_[9]_
(E)_[10]_
(F)_[11]_
(G)_[12]_
(H)_[13]_

of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 14 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 and section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order
Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) From 28th June 2022 this offence was extended to cover the commission of an offence under sections 5 to 13 of the Act; for offences committed after that date the penalty differs depending on the offence attempted to arrange or facilitate.
(ii) For the full offence see H5719.
(iii) Provided the victim was under 16, an act done by a person in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom which constituted an offence under the law in force in that country or territory, and would constitute a sexual offence to which this section applies if it had been done in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland, constitutes that sexual offence under the law of that part of the United Kingdom, and provided that person was on 1st September 1997, or who has since become a British citizen or resident in the United Kingdom he or she may have proceedings brought against them in the United Kingdom, section 72.
(iv) A person convicted of this offence who was aged 18 or over or sentenced in respect of this offence to at least twelve months imprisonment is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act (Schedule 3, paragraph 23).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction was increased from 2nd May 2022, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003. This applies only to offences committed on or after that date, see section 282(4). For offences committed before 2nd May 2022 the maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
